data.narrative:
Exolaunch, a bootstrapped Space & Aerospace company founded by Dmitriy Sternharz and Dmitriy Bogdanov (both TU Berlin space technology alumni), operates within a sector containing 13 identifiable peers—5 public (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private (including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs). The company's early stage and nascent revenue profile limit traditional valuation anchors.

Peer-median triangulation is not applicable; the 14 same-sector peers do not yield three or more datapoints when filtered by stage, timing, or valuation tier. Public-comp anchoring cannot proceed: while the Space & Aerospace sector trades at a median P/S of 27.4x across the six public comparables identified, Exolaunch's revenue is not disclosed, rendering the multiple inapplicable. Standard venture pricing methods—diluted DCF, precedent transaction, and forward-revenue multiples—similarly cannot be deployed without revenue guidance or recent fundraising data.

The absence of both a viable peer set and target financials forecloses quantitative valuation support at this time. Any valuation would rest on qualitative factors: founding team pedigree, intellectual property in launch logistics, and sector momentum. The analyst should await either revenue disclosure, a contemporaneous financing event, or identification of additional bootstrapped Space & Aerospace comparables before reassessing. Current data is insufficient to produce a credible range.
